title: Graded sheaf modules form a Grothendieck category
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra. Use left sheaf dg modules and signed shifts as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Write $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$ for the category whose objects are integer-graded $\mathcal O$-module sheaves $N=\bigoplus_n N^n$ with associative unital graded left action $\mathcal A^i\otimes_{\mathcal O}N^j\to N^{i+j}$, without any differential on $N$; its maps are action-preserving maps of degree zero. Then $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian].

source.place: Tag 0FRD (lemma-gm-grothendieck-abelian), with Tag 0FR0 (lemma-gm-abelian); left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: Work on the small open site of $X$. The cited ordinary module category is abelian; its kernels are sectionwise and its cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels. For $f:M\to N$ of degree zero, put $K^q=\ker f^q$ and $C^q=\operatorname{coker}f^q$ in that category. The identity $f(am)=af(m)$ restricts the action to $K$. For $C$, tensor-colimit preservation makes $\mathcal A^i\otimes C^q$ the cokernel of $\mathcal A^i\otimes M^q\to\mathcal A^i\otimes N^q$. The composite to $C^{i+q}$ kills that map and hence induces the quotient action. Its unit and associativity follow from those on $N$ by precomposing with these epimorphic quotient maps, tensoring twice for associativity. Degreewise kernel and cokernel factorizations preserve actions by the same identities, so they have the graded universal properties. Addition, zero and finite biproducts are componentwise. The canonical coimage-to-image map is an isomorphism in every degree, since ordinary module sheaves are abelian. Its inverse respects the action by composing the action square with the degreewise inverses. Thus the graded category is abelian. This also shows that a sequence is exact precisely when it is exact in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0FR0 (lemma-gm-abelian), kernel and cokernel paragraph; quotient actions expressed using Tag 03EP (sites-modules-lemma-tensor-commute-colimits).

proof.text: For any small diagram $(M_t)$, take $Q^q=\operatorname{colim}_t M_t^q$ in ordinary module sheaves, with maps $c_t^q$. Such colimits exist by the cited ordinary Grothendieck assertion. Tensor-colimit preservation gives the unique maps $\mu_{i,q}:\mathcal A^i\otimes Q^q\to Q^{i+q}$ satisfying $\mu_{i,q}(1\otimes c_t^q)=c_t^{i+q}\mu^t_{i,q}$. The unit identity follows after precomposing with every $c_t^q$. The two associativity composites from $\mathcal A^i\otimes\mathcal A^j\otimes Q^q$ agree after precomposing with $1\otimes1\otimes c_t^q$, because the actions on $M_t$ are associative; these maps jointly determine a morphism by two applications of tensor-colimit preservation. Hence $Q$ is a graded module. Given a graded cocone to $T$, its unique degreewise factorization $Q^q\to T^q$ respects actions by testing after $1\otimes c_t^q$. This proves the colimit universal property, including the empty diagram. Thus all small colimits exist and are computed degreewise.

source.place: Tag 0FR0 (lemma-gm-abelian), colimit paragraphs; direct construction of arbitrary colimits using Tag 03EP.

proof.text: For a small filtered diagram of short exact sequences of graded modules, step 1 makes each degree a diagram of short exact sequences of ordinary $\mathcal O$-module sheaves. Their colimit sequence is exact by the cited ordinary Grothendieck assertion. Step 2 identifies this sequence in each degree with the corresponding degree of the graded colimit sequence. Applying degreewise detection of exactness from step 1 proves exactness of filtered colimits in $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0FR0 (lemma-gm-abelian), final paragraph; ordinary input sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A5, section-unbounded.

proof.text: For an open $U$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, let $F_{U,n}$ be the underlying graded left module of the signed shift $\mathcal A_U[-n]$. Explicitly $F_{U,n}^q=\mathcal A_U^{q-n}$, and $a\cdot b=(-1)^{n|a|}ab$. Ignore its differential. For any graded $M$, evaluation at $1$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A_U)}(F_{U,n},M|_U)\simeq\Gamma(U,M^n)$. Indeed, a section $m$ has inverse map $b\mapsto(-1)^{n|b|}bm$ on each open inside $U$. It respects restrictions and is degree zero. For homogeneous $a,b$ its value on $a\cdot b$ is $(-1)^{n|a|+n(|a|+|b|)}abm=(-1)^{n|b|}abm$, which equals $a$ times the value on $b$. Conversely $b=(-1)^{n|b|}(b\cdot1)$ forces this formula for every linear map; evaluation at $1$ returns $m$. The cited graded extension adjunction now yields a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)}(j_{U!}F_{U,n},M)\simeq\Gamma(U,M^n)$.

source.place: Tag 0FRD (lemma-gm-grothendieck-abelian), displayed Hom calculation; Tag 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded), with signed left shift and its explicit evaluation formula.

proof.text: The opens $U$ and integers $n$ form a set in the chosen universe. Form $G=\bigoplus_{U,n}j_{U!}F_{U,n}$ using step 2. To prove that $\operatorname{Hom}(G,-)$ is faithful, take distinct maps $f,g:M\to N$. Some degree $n$, open $U$ and section $m\in M^n(U)$ satisfy $f(m)\ne g(m)$, since maps of sheaves are determined by sections. Step 4 supplies $h:j_{U!}F_{U,n}\to M$ corresponding to $m$, and by naturality $fh\ne gh$. Extend $h$ to $G$ by assigning zero to every other summand. The composites with $f$ and $g$ remain distinct on this summand. Thus $G$ is a generator. Abelianness from step 1, small colimits from step 2, exact filtered colimits from step 3, and this generator give precisely the cited definition of Grothendieck abelian.

source.place: Tag 0FRD (lemma-gm-grothendieck-abelian), generator paragraph; faithfulness verified directly on distinct maps, strengthening the source's zero-object detection argument.
